title: I Reported the Flea-Market Scale After They Zeroed With a Thumb

parts.text: I bought tomatoes at 9:44 a.m. and the scale hopped from 1.8 to 2.4 when a thumb landed. The market rule on the stall pole said: SCALES IN VIEW. NO HAND ON THE PLATE. I was thirty-five, Saturday shopper, holding a receipt that already looked heavy. Vendor Cal said, "Wind." There was no wind. I pointed at the pole. He laughed. "Stalls are weather." I photographed the thumb, the pole, and the two readings. Then I reported the stall number to the market office with both stills. At 9:51 the manager asked why Cal's stall was on a scale-tamper ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The market office can see a thumb on the plate against the pole rule.

social.video_title: The stall called a thumb the wind — Part 1/2
social.description: Tomatoes, two readings, and a pole rule. I reported the stall. Would you have paid the 2.4?

parts.text: Cal called it a joke until the office recertified the scale. I printed the ticket, the pole photo, and the readings. They refunded the jump. Cal weighed with hands visible and told the aisle the pole was always about optics. Optics is a word vendors use when a thumb is in 4K. Stall policy now has a second line: WIND IS NOT A THUMB. I buy by the reading. Cal keeps palms up. The plate finally sits still.

social.video_title: Wind is not a thumb on the plate — Part 2/2
social.description: Tamper ticket, a refund, and a second line on the pole. Was weather ever 0.6 pounds?
